name: venus_audit_2032_original_failure
description: The original Earth-Venus-Mars audit failure: required turn far exceeds Venus's physical deflection ceiling for this approach speed. Computed using v_inf = 13.355 km/s to match the actual audit conditions.

name: earth_grazing_extreme_turn
description: An Earth flyby demanding a near-180° turn at typical interplanetary approach speed — should fail even the unlimited-burn ceiling test, since asin(1/e_in)+90° still has a finite bound for any e_in > 1.

name: mercury_modest_turn_should_pass
description: A CONTROL case — a modest, clearly achievable turn at Mercury, included to prove the bank also correctly ACCEPTS reasonable geometry, not just rejects everything.

name: jupiter_voyager_class_large_turn
description: A large but historically-realistic turn angle at Jupiter (Voyager-class flybys achieved tens of degrees of deflection at large v_inf using Jupiter's enormous μ) — included as a control case proving the bank doesn't falsely reject large-but-real planetary deflections.

name: mars_infeasible_extreme_turn
description: A Mars flyby requiring a 120-degree turn at 6 km/s. The unpowered ceiling is 28.83 degrees and the powered ceiling is 104.41 degrees, making this case completely infeasible.

name: saturn_feasible_modest_turn
description: A Saturn flyby requiring a 35-degree turn at 15 km/s. The unpowered ceiling is 94.62 degrees, making this case fully achievable without any burn.
